clues.clue: Historically a discrete chipset, this function is now integrated into the CPU die itself and connects the CPU to RAM and high-speed PCIe expansion slots.
clues.response: What is the Northbridge (today the integrated memory controller)?
clues.explain: In modern architectures, the memory controller is integrated directly into the CPU die (since Intel Sandy Bridge and AMD Ryzen). Historically, the Northbridge chipset handled this function. The term persists in the A+ curriculum to describe the high-speed data path between CPU, RAM, and PCIe slots.

clues.clue: Two DDR4 modules only run in dual-channel mode when installed in slots marked this way on the motherboard -- the manual tells you which pairs qualify.
clues.response: What are matching color-coded slots (the paired dual-channel slots)?
clues.explain: Dual-channel memory requires modules to be installed in paired slots, typically indicated by matching colors on the motherboard (e.g., both blue slots or both black slots). The motherboard manual specifies which slots form a dual-channel pair. Incorrect placement results in single-channel operation, reducing memory bandwidth.

clues.clue: A workstation powers on with no video, sounding one long beep and three short beeps from its AMI BIOS -- the beep code that points to a failure of this component.
clues.explain: One long beep followed by three short beeps in AMI BIOS typically indicates a video card/GPU failure or the video card is not properly seated. The technician should reseat the graphics card, check power connections to the GPU, and test with a known-good card.

clues.clue: For a build whose 300W GPU needs two 8-pin PCIe connectors plus five SATA drives, this minimum PSU wattage -- with an 80 Plus Gold rating -- covers total system draw plus 20-30% headroom.
clues.explain: With a 300W GPU, ~125W CPU, ~50W for drives and motherboard, the system draws approximately 475W under load. Adding 20-30% headroom for transient spikes and component aging brings the recommendation to 600-650W. 80 Plus Gold (87-90% efficiency at typical loads) means less waste heat and lower electricity costs compared to Bronze (82-85%).

clues.clue: Four PCIe Gen 4 NVMe SSDs -- roughly 12x faster than SATA III -- deliver maximum sustained 4K video throughput while keeping fault tolerance when striped and mirrored in this RAID level.
clues.explain: PCIe Gen 4 x4 NVMe drives achieve up to ~7,000 MB/s sequential read vs. SATA III maximum of 600 MB/s (approximately 12x faster). RAID 10 with four NVMe drives provides striped reads/writes across mirrored pairs: near-RAID 0 performance with single-drive fault tolerance per mirror pair. RAID 5 with NVMe can cause write amplification issues with SSDs, making RAID 10 the preferred choice for this use case.

clues.clue: Per the TIA/EIA-568 standard, this is the maximum length for a single run of Cat 6 Ethernet cable, patch cables included.
clues.explain: 100 meters (328 feet) is the maximum supported cable length for a single run of Cat 5e, Cat 6, or Cat 6a cable per the TIA/EIA-568 standard. This includes patch cables at both ends. Exceeding this distance causes signal degradation and packet loss.

clues.clue: This is the number of usable host addresses on the 192.168.1.0/24 subnet, once the network and broadcast addresses are subtracted.
clues.explain: A /24 subnet (255.255.255.0) provides 256 total addresses (2^8). Subtract 2: the network address (192.168.1.0) and the broadcast address (192.168.1.255) are not assignable to hosts, leaving 254 usable host addresses.

clues.clue: A workstation pings its gateway fine, but no website loads and nslookup fails -- the misconfiguration or outage of this service is the most likely cause.
clues.explain: The workstation has valid IP connectivity (can ping gateway) but cannot resolve names. Since nslookup also fails, the DNS configuration is the issue: either the DNS server IP is wrong, the DNS server is down, or firewall rules are blocking DNS (UDP/TCP port 53). The network layer is functioning correctly.

clues.clue: Floor 1 sits on VLAN 10 and Floor 2 on VLAN 20, and they cannot talk to each other; this class of device performs the inter-VLAN routing that fixes it.
clues.response: What is a Layer 3 switch (or a router configured for inter-VLAN routing)?
clues.explain: VLANs create separate broadcast domains at Layer 2. Communication between VLANs requires Layer 3 routing. A Layer 3 switch with SVIs (Switch Virtual Interfaces) for each VLAN, or a router connected via trunk port (router-on-a-stick), can route traffic between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.

clues.clue: Port forwarding on a SOHO router fails because the ISP-assigned WAN IP is in the 100.64.x.x range -- this carrier-side technology has put the user behind double NAT.
clues.explain: The 100.64.0.0/10 range (RFC 6598) is reserved for CGNAT (Carrier-Grade NAT), meaning the ISP assigns a private-like address to the customer router and performs NAT at the ISP level. Port forwarding on the home router only works for the first NAT layer; the ISP NAT blocks inbound connections. The user needs a public IP from the ISP (often a paid upgrade) or must use a tunneling service.

clues.clue: With a range of only about 4 centimeters, this connection type is the standard behind contactless payments like Apple Pay and Google Pay.
clues.explain: NFC operates at a range of approximately 4 cm (1.5 inches) and is used for contactless payments (Apple Pay, Google Pay), transit cards, and device pairing. Its extremely short range provides inherent security against remote interception.

clues.clue: This technology separates corporate data from personal data on a smartphone, enforces encryption, and lets admins remotely wipe only the work container.
clues.explain: MDM solutions (Intune, Workspace ONE, MobileIron) create separate containers for corporate and personal data. Administrators can enforce encryption policies, remotely wipe the corporate container without touching personal data, and manage application deployment within the work profile.

clues.clue: Troubleshooting a phone that dies in 3 hours starts by checking this metric in settings, before reviewing per-app usage, disabling background refresh, and testing in safe mode.
clues.explain: Systematic troubleshooting begins with checking battery health (iOS: Settings > Battery > Battery Health; Android: Settings > Battery). Next, identify apps with abnormal battery consumption. Disabling background refresh for non-essential apps reduces idle drain. Safe mode isolates whether a third-party app is the culprit. Battery replacement is a last resort for a 6-month-old device.

clues.clue: This Microsoft protocol delivers push email with calendar and contact synchronization to smartphones, over HTTPS on port 443.
clues.explain: Exchange ActiveSync (EAS) is Microsoft's protocol for synchronizing email, calendar, contacts, and tasks with mobile devices. It uses HTTPS (port 443) for encrypted communication and supports push notifications for real-time email delivery. POP3 and IMAP can access email but do not natively synchronize calendars and contacts.

clues.clue: A factory reset only makes encrypted data truly unrecoverable when it performs this key-destroying operation -- which NIST 800-88 decommissioning requires you to verify.
clues.explain: Modern devices with hardware-backed encryption perform a cryptographic erase during factory reset (destroying the encryption key, making data unrecoverable). However, older devices or those with software-based encryption may not securely overwrite all storage blocks. Proper NIST 800-88 compliant decommissioning verifies the erase type, performs validation testing, and documents the process. Physical destruction is reserved for highest-security classifications.

clues.clue: This software or firmware layer creates and manages virtual machines -- Type 1 runs on bare metal, Type 2 runs on top of a host OS.
clues.explain: A hypervisor (also called a Virtual Machine Monitor) is the layer that abstracts physical hardware and allocates resources to virtual machines. Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on hardware (ESXi, Hyper-V). Type 2 (hosted) hypervisors run on top of an operating system (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation).

clues.clue: Of the three major cloud service models, this one delivers complete ready-to-use applications, abstracting the most management responsibility away from the customer.
clues.response: What is SaaS (Software as a Service)?
clues.explain: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides VMs, storage, and networking. PaaS (Platform as a Service) adds managed runtime environments, databases, and development tools. SaaS (Software as a Service) delivers complete applications. Moving from IaaS to SaaS, the cloud provider manages increasingly more of the stack.

clues.clue: Three 4-vCPU virtual machines fighting over an 8-core host rack up CPU ready time and degraded performance -- the classic symptom of this condition.
clues.explain: With 12 vCPUs competing for 8 physical cores, the hypervisor scheduler must time-slice physical CPU access. When multiple VMs need CPU simultaneously, they experience "CPU ready" time (waiting for a physical core). VM performance degrades during contention periods. The ratio of vCPUs to physical cores (1.5:1 here) should be monitored and kept within acceptable bounds based on workload patterns.

clues.clue: A legacy app that demands a specific OS kernel version and custom kernel modules should migrate to the cloud under this service model, deployed from a custom VM image.
clues.response: What is IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)?
clues.explain: IaaS provides the most control over the operating system environment. The company can build a custom VM image with the exact kernel version and modules required, upload it to the cloud provider, and deploy VMs from that image. PaaS and SaaS abstract the OS layer, and serverless does not provide kernel-level access.

clues.clue: To meet a 15-minute RPO and 1-hour RTO, you continuously replicate the database to this kind of always-running standby VM in another region, with automated failover.
clues.response: What is a hot standby (hot site)?
clues.explain: The 15-minute RPO requires data replication or backups at least every 15 minutes. Continuous replication provides near-zero RPO, and 15-minute incremental backups provide point-in-time recovery. The 1-hour RTO requires the standby to be running or quickly startable; a hot standby with automated failover meets this easily. Daily snapshots (24-hour RPO) and weekly tapes violate the RPO. A pilot light configuration may exceed the 1-hour RTO due to server boot and data sync time.

clues.clue: Faded print on every page coming out of a laser printer points first to this component running low.
clues.explain: Consistently faded output across all pages is the most common symptom of low toner. The toner cartridge should be checked first. Gently rocking the cartridge side-to-side can redistribute remaining toner temporarily, but replacement is needed. Fuser issues typically cause smearing, not fading.

clues.clue: Random shutdowns under heavy load that stop happening once the machine cools down are the classic signature of this condition.
clues.explain: Random shutdowns under load that resolve after cooling are classic thermal shutdown symptoms. Modern CPUs and GPUs have thermal protection that forces shutdown when temperatures exceed safe thresholds (typically 100-105C for CPUs). Common causes include dust-clogged heatsinks, dried thermal paste, or failed case fans.

clues.clue: BIOS detects the new NVMe SSD but Windows setup cannot see it -- you fix this with this installer option and the manufacturer's storage driver on a USB stick.
clues.explain: Older Windows installation media may not include drivers for newer NVMe controllers or RAID controllers. During Windows setup, the "Load driver" option allows loading the appropriate storage controller driver from a USB drive. The manufacturer provides these drivers on their support website. This is especially common with custom OEM NVMe controllers.

clues.clue: Varying memory-related BSOD codes on RAM that passes a quick test but fails this longer kind of test indicate intermittent bit errors -- isolate the bad stick by testing modules individually.
clues.response: What is an extended (stress) memory test?
clues.explain: Multiple memory-related BSOD stop codes combined with passing quick RAM tests but failing extended tests indicate marginal RAM with intermittent bit errors. Quick tests only check basic addressing; extended tests stress-test every cell with patterns that reveal subtle failures. Testing each module individually (in the same known-good slot) isolates the faulty module.

clues.clue: Fans at full speed with no video and no beeps right after a CPU upgrade means the CPU never starts executing code -- before suspecting the board, verify bent pins, the EPS power connector, and this firmware-level compatibility factor.
clues.response: What is BIOS/UEFI support for the new CPU (BIOS revision compatibility)?
clues.explain: Fans at full speed with no POST/beep indicates the system is not entering POST code execution, pointing to a CPU initialization failure. After a CPU upgrade, the most likely causes are: (1) BIOS version does not support the new CPU (common with newer CPUs on older boards), (2) bent socket/CPU pins from installation, (3) the 4/8-pin CPU power connector is not seated. Testing with the original CPU confirms whether the issue is CPU compatibility or socket damage.
